tagline: Bridging the gap between families and food assistance
demo_help: Loads fictional information so you can explore every feature safely.
data_cleared: Your session information has been cleared.
independent_notice: Independent preparation tool — not a government website
government_disclaimer: SNAPBridge does not submit an application or determine eligibility. Only the Arizona Department of Economic Security can make an official decision.
hero_title: A clearer path to food assistance starts here.
hero_body: Answer plain-language questions, understand possible eligibility pathways, organize documents, and prepare to apply through Arizona’s official portal.
privacy_body: We don't save your answers to a database or account. They are kept temporarily for this session and cleared when the session ends.
adaptive_body: You only see follow-up questions that match your household’s circumstances.
explainable_body: Every screening result shows the rule, date, and official source behind it.
workflow_title: From uncertainty to a prepared next step
workflow_5: Apply on the official Arizona portal
supported_state: Currently available for Arizona only. We are adding more states.
state_help: SNAP is administered by each state. Arizona is the only verified state in this release.
household_size: How many people buy and prepare food together in your household?
household_help: A SNAP household is usually people who live together and purchase and prepare meals together. Some relationships must be included under official rules.
children: How many household members are under age 18?
older_disabled: Does anyone applying have a qualifying disability or is age 60 or older?
older_disabled_help: This can change which income test and medical deductions Arizona uses. DES makes the official determination.
employment: Which description best fits the household?
income_prompt: Does anyone in your household receive money from work, self-employment, retirement, unemployment, child support, Social Security, or another source?
income_amount: About how much gross income does the household receive at this frequency?
gross_help: Gross means before taxes or other deductions. Use an estimate for this preparation screen.
income_frequency: How often is that amount received?
expense_intro: Expenses do not change the gross screen shown here, but Arizona may use allowable deductions in its official net-income calculation.
childcare: Monthly dependent-care expenses needed for work or school
medical: Monthly out-of-pocket medical expenses for older/disabled members
validation_error: Please correct the highlighted information before continuing.
result_may_qualify: Your household may pass Arizona’s standard gross-income screen
result_needs_review: Arizona needs more information to screen this household reliably
result_des_confirm: You may qualify. DES will calculate the final answer.
result_older_body: Because someone applying is age 60 or older or has a qualifying disability, Arizona uses a different income review. You did not miss a question.
result_unlikely_income: Reported income is above the expanded gross-income screen
result_unsupported: Unable to determine for this state
explain_under_130: The estimated monthly gross income is at or below Arizona’s 130% FPL standard for this household size.
explain_between_limits: Income is above the standard 130% screen but within Arizona’s 200% expanded categorical limit. Extra program conditions determine whether that pathway applies.
explain_over_200: Income is above Arizona’s 200% expanded categorical limit for this household size. Special rules or excluded income may still matter, so this is not a denial.
explain_net_only: Arizona generally does not apply the gross-income test to a budgetary unit containing an older adult or qualifying disabled participant; an official net-income calculation is needed.
explain_net_only_plain: The usual 130% income limit is not used for this household. DES will review income and allowed expenses instead.
explain_apply_unsure: You can apply even if you are not sure. DES makes the decision.
explain_official_decision_plain: Only Arizona DES can decide whether you qualify and how much help you may receive.
explain_net_test: Passing a gross screen does not establish eligibility. Arizona also reviews countable income, allowable deductions, household rules, and other program requirements.
explain_official_decision: Only Arizona DES can make the official eligibility and benefit decision after an application and interview.
explain_only_arizona: This version contains verified rules only for Arizona.
assistant_intro: We reuse your screening answers and ask only for details that help build your worksheet. Do not enter Social Security numbers, bank credentials, or document images.
why_household: Arizona uses who buys and prepares food together to form the SNAP budgetary unit.
why_income: DES reviews money received and allowable expenses to complete official income tests.
older_disabled_review_help: This means a person included in this SNAP application, not anyone else who happens to live at the address. DES decides whether a disability meets program rules.
documents_intro: Arizona says these items may be needed. Your exact verification request can differ; provide copies rather than originals when instructed by DES.
reason_identity: DES lists identity and citizenship verification among information that may be needed for people applying.
example_identity: Examples: government-issued photo ID, birth certificate, or other DES-accepted proof. Do not upload it to SNAPBridge.
reason_residency: Your state and living arrangement affect which agency handles the application.
example_residency: Examples listed by DES include a signed address statement or current mail. DES decides what is acceptable.
doc_income: Income received this month and last month
example_income: Examples: recent pay stubs, benefit letters, employer statement, or self-employment records.
reason_housing: You reported a housing payment that may be relevant to an allowable shelter deduction.
example_housing: Examples: lease, rent receipt, mortgage statement, or landlord statement.
example_utilities: Examples: recent electric, water, or gas bill and information about home heating or cooling.
reason_childcare: You reported care costs connected with work or school.
example_childcare: Example: provider statement or receipt for the most recent month.
reason_medical: You reported more than $35 in medical costs and an older/disabled household member.
example_medical: Examples: bills, receipts, prescription costs, insurance premiums, or approved transportation records.
example_child_support: Examples: court order and proof of recent payments.
reason_notes: A short question list can help you get answers during the required interview.
example_notes: Note anything unusual about income, household members, or documents you cannot obtain.
readiness_disclaimer: This score measures preparation steps completed. It is not the chance of approval.
all_ready: Your preparation worksheet is ready to use with the official application.
pdf_download_warning: This PDF contains personal details. Save or print it carefully, especially on a shared or library computer.
pdf_personal_details_warning: Privacy reminder: This file contains personal details. Delete it from shared or library computers and collect printed copies.
not_application_disclaimer: This worksheet was prepared by an independent tool. It has not been submitted to a government agency and is not an eligibility decision or government-approved form.
portal_notice: You are leaving SNAPBridge for Arizona’s official application system.
privacy_short: SNAPBridge generated this file in memory. It does not retain your responses after your session is cleared or expires.
faq_what_a: SNAP is a federal nutrition program administered in Arizona as Nutrition Assistance. Eligible households receive benefits to buy food from authorized retailers.
faq_who_a: Anyone may submit an application. Arizona DES evaluates household composition, residency, income, deductions, and other program rules. Applying is the only way to receive an official decision.
faq_income_a: Arizona reviews countable earned and unearned income. The treatment of a particular source can vary, so report it to DES and let the agency determine whether it counts.
faq_docs_a: DES may request identity, residency, income, housing, utilities, childcare, medical, or child-support information depending on your household. Your checklist adapts to the answers you provide.
faq_apply: How do I apply in Arizona?
faq_apply_a: Apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus, or follow Arizona DES instructions for mail, fax, in-person help, or a Community Assistor.
faq_after_a: Arizona requires an eligibility interview and may request additional verification. DES says decisions are generally made within 30 days, or within 7 days for households qualifying for emergency benefits.
faq_missing_doc: What if I cannot provide a document?
faq_missing_doc_a: Tell your DES eligibility specialist as soon as possible. Arizona DES says it can assist when requested information is hard to obtain.
how_to_apply: How to apply and what may be needed
interview_hours: Telephone interviews are available Monday through Friday, except state holidays, from 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
language_help: Free language assistance is available. Call DES and ask for an interpreter in your preferred language.
about_title: Built to make a hard process feel manageable
problem_body: SNAP rules and application steps can be hard to understand, especially when a family is already worried about food, time, transportation, or paperwork.
motivation_body: We wanted families to have a calm, plain-language guide that explains why each question matters and helps them prepare before they enter Arizona's official system.
mission_body: SNAPBridge turns application preparation into clear, explainable steps while sending every official action back to the responsible state agency.
technology_body: Python, Streamlit, configuration-driven rules, local session state, ReportLab PDF generation, and automated tests. No paid services or API keys.
privacy_body_long: The public MVP uses temporary per-session memory. It does not ask for Social Security numbers, bank credentials, or document uploads; it does not write responses to shared storage; and it does not send answers to an external AI service. Clearing the session deletes the in-memory answers. Downloaded files are controlled by the user.
limitations_body: Arizona is the only configured state. The screener does not calculate countable net income, benefit amounts, student eligibility, immigration eligibility, work requirements, resources, or every categorical rule. Uncertain cases are deliberately referred to DES.
challenge_body: This student civic-technology project demonstrates adaptive questions, explainable rules, tailored document preparation, bilingual access, and privacy-first design.
ai_use_body: We used generative AI to help scaffold code, draft interface copy and tests, and find official sources. We then checked the eligibility rules against USDA and Arizona DES sources, ran our automated tests, reviewed the design and translations, and documented where AI helped.
contest_rule_ai: AI tools are allowed when they are fully disclosed, support rather than replace the students' work, and students make significant contributions and understand the app.
contest_rule_team: A team may have up to four eligible students, and at least half must live or attend school in the participating district.
contest_rule_video: The public demo video must be 1–3 minutes and include the students' names, app name and purpose, intended audience, tools or languages used, and a demonstration of the app.
contest_rule_deadline: The 2026 submission deadline is October 26, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time.
